capability_investigated:
The feature-extraction + batched-decode path: processor() always pads/
truncates audio to one 30s (3000-frame) mel window, and generate() accepts a
batched feature view (N,80,3000) paired with one prompt per item.
what_i_learned:
The stub's single processor() call hard-caps coverage at the first 30s, so on
multi-minute 0715 calls almost the entire reference is deleted (length_ratio
floored). generate() decodes N stacked windows in a single call, so full-file
coverage costs one batched decode per file rather than N sequential calls.
hypothesis:
Slice audio into consecutive 30s windows, stack their mel features, decode the
whole batch at once, and join the per-window text. This directly attacks the
dominant deletion axis by transcribing the tail the stub threw away, while the
batched call keeps runtime inside the budget.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s batch dimension vs GPU memory: how peak CUDA allocation scales
with the number of stacked (80,3000) mel windows passed in one decode call.
what_i_learned:
generate() does NOT stream the batch — passing all N windows of a multi-minute
file as one (N,80,3000) view makes the whole batch resident on the GPU at once
and OOMs. The batch dimension is bounded by VRAM, not just by API acceptance;
one-window-per-call keeps peak memory flat at single-window size.
hypothesis:
Keep the full-file 30s windowing that fixes the deletion/length_ratio floor,
but decode each window in its own generate() call instead of one batched call,
so coverage no longer trades against an OOM crash.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s beam_size decoding kwarg on the per-window decode path — how the
CT2 Whisper search width changes within-window coverage versus the greedy
(beam_size=1) decode the parent uses.
what_i_learned:
The parent already covers the full audio (every 30s window is decoded), yet
length_ratio is only 0.65 and repeated_text fires on 4/12 files. So the
deletion is intra-window, not coverage-of-audio: greedy beam=1 decode collapses
into repetition loops / early EOS inside a window and strands the rest of that
window's speech. CT2 generate() does NOT auto-fallback on temperature, so beam
width is the available robustness lever against greedy collapse.
hypothesis:
Raise beam_size 1->5 on the per-window decode. Wider beam search avoids the
greedy looping/early-termination that deletes the tail of each window, lifting
length_ratio and cutting repeated_text against the dominant deletion axis;
~5x of 103.8s inference still fits the 719.9s budget.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s return object beyond sequences_ids — the return_scores and
return_no_speech_prob decoding kwargs, and what WhisperGenerationResult
exposes (scores = length-normalised log-prob of the chosen hypothesis,
no_speech_prob) that the pipeline currently discards.
what_i_learned:
generate() will populate result.scores (a length-normalised mean log-prob,
reference-comparable to Whisper's avg_logprob ~-1.0 threshold) and
no_speech_prob when asked, so the decoder's own confidence is readable per
window. Combined with gzip compression ratio of the decoded text, that gives
the exact two-signal degeneracy test Whisper uses — meaning manual
temperature fallback (which iter_003 found CT2 does NOT do automatically) is
fully implementable on the frozen surface.
hypothesis:
Intra-window collapse (iter_003: repetition loops / early EOS strand a
window's tail → deletion 82%) is curable by re-decoding only the degenerate
windows at escalating temperature. Gate retries on scores < -1.0 OR
compression_ratio > 2.4 so healthy windows stay at one beam=5 decode; failing
windows escalate T=0→1.0 with full-vocab sampling, recovering stranded speech
and raising length_ratio without inflating runtime.

capability_investigated:
result.no_speech_prob on the WhisperGenerationResult — already populated via
return_no_speech_prob=True since iter_004 but never read — as Whisper's
reference non-speech detector, paired with result.scores[0].
what_i_learned:
family_002 and family_001 share the beam=5 base; family_002's only added
mechanism (temperature fallback) is precisely what raised hallucination
0.18→0.27, because on near-silent windows it escalates to full-distribution
sampling (topk=0) and hallucinates. no_speech_prob is the discarded signal
that flags those windows before escalation, so the deletion-recovery of
family_002 and the lower-hallucination behaviour of family_001 can coexist:
detect degeneracy via compression+logprob, but gate the sampling escalation
behind a silence check.
hypothesis:
Graft both: keep family_002's beam=5 + compression/logprob temperature
fallback (deletion axis), and guard the hallucination axis it regressed by
returning "" when no_speech_prob > 0.6 AND scores[0] < -1.0 — Whisper's exact
non-speech rule — so silent windows are skipped instead of sampled into
invented text. Conservative thresholds keep speech-heavy high-deletion files
(length_ratio 0.51–0.58, low no_speech) untouched.

capability_investigated:
Whisper timestamp tokens on the generate() path: removing <|notimestamps|>
from the prompt so result.sequences_ids carries <|t|> tokens (ids >=
convert_tokens_to_ids("<|0.00|>"), 0.02s steps), and what the last
segment-end timestamp says about how far the 30s window was consumed.
what_i_learned:
The frozen surface supports timestamp decoding: the prompt without
<|notimestamps|> lets the model emit timestamp tokens in sequences_ids, and
their value (id - timestamp_begin) * 0.02 gives the consumed-time of each
window — a per-window seek signal the fixed-stride pipeline never had.
length_ratio sits at ~0.65 on EVERY file (even flagless ones, e.g. 0.81/0.74
best-cases), so the deletion is a systematic boundary loss from blind 30s
cuts, not just the degenerate-window collapse iter_003 isolated.
hypothesis:
Decode with timestamps and advance the next window to the last segment-end
timestamp instead of a blind +30s. Utterances straddling a boundary are then
re-decoded whole from the next window's start rather than truncated, lifting
coverage/length_ratio against the dominant deletion axis; healthy windows
reaching ~30s still take a full stride so added decode cost is bounded.

capability_investigated:
The two generate() calls in _decode_window and which of their return-value
flags the gating logic actually consumes: result.scores[0] (logprob) and the
gzip compression ratio of the decoded text are read; result.no_speech_prob,
populated by return_no_speech_prob=True, is never read anywhere.
what_i_learned:
return_no_speech_prob=True is a pure dead override on the mature pipeline:
it populates result.no_speech_prob but the degeneracy gate uses only
compression_ratio<=2.4 AND avg_logprob>=-1.0. Requesting it cannot change
sequences_ids or text, so removing it is CER-neutral by construction — the
signal iter_005 proposed gating on was never actually wired in.
hypothesis:
ABLATE: remove return_no_speech_prob=True from both generate() calls. The
decode output and gating are unchanged, so CER holds while the call surface
is simpler and one unused per-window return computation is dropped.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s prompts argument as a writable input, not just the fixed
[sot, lang, task] triple — specifically the <|startofprev|> token slot that
Whisper reserves before <|startoftranscript|> for previous-text conditioning
(condition_on_previous_text), and whether CT2 honors arbitrary prepended ids.
what_i_learned:
The prompt is a flat token-id list fully under workspace control: prepending
[startofprev, *prev_text_tokens, sot, lang, task] is accepted by generate()
and conditions the decode on prior context. This is an input-side lever
distinct from every prior finding (all of which read decode *outputs* —
scores, no_speech_prob, timestamps — or widened search). It directly targets
substitution, which coverage/timestamp work cannot, since it changes *what*
the decoder recognizes (domain terms, cross-boundary continuations) rather
than how much audio is consumed.
hypothesis:
With length_ratio healthy (0.96) and substitution now 56% of error, prime each
window with the running call context via <|startofprev|> + the last 224 text
tokens, reset after a degeneracy-gate failure so a repetition loop cannot
poison later prompts. Consistent domain vocabulary across the ~80 windows/file
should lower substitution without affecting coverage.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s no_repeat_ngram_size decoding kwarg — a logit-processor-level
constraint applied during the search step that hard-bans re-emitting any
n-gram already produced in the hypothesis. Distinct from the compression-ratio
health check, which only detects a repetition loop after it has already been
decoded and then pays for a full temperature-fallback re-decode.
what_i_learned:
The frozen generate() surface exposes decode-time repetition control, not just
the post-hoc detect-and-redecode path the pipeline uses now. no_repeat_ngram_size
is an unused logit constraint orthogonal to beam_size (search width), the
temperature schedule (sampling), timestamps (coverage), and the prompt slot
(input conditioning) — it shapes the per-step distribution so a verbatim loop
cannot form, rather than scoring a finished hypothesis. This is the first
in-search robustness lever probed; all prior findings read outputs or widened
search after the fact.
hypothesis:
Banning repeated trigrams (size 3) on both the beam and sampling decode calls
should clear the repeated_text guard violations on focus files 1065 and 8016
before the compression gate ever fires, removing the repetition-driven
insertions/substitutions inside those loops while leaving healthy windows
(where exact trigram repeats are rare in natural Korean call speech) untouched.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s beam-search `patience` decoding kwarg on the temperature=0.0
path — distinct from beam_size (search width, probed iter_003). Patience is
the CT2/Whisper factor controlling how many finished hypotheses the beam
search collects (≈ beam_size * patience) before finalizing, i.e. how long
alternative beams stay alive before the best is committed.
what_i_learned:
The frozen generate() surface accepts `patience` independently of beam_size,
so beam exploration depth is tunable without widening the beam itself. This
is an in-search hypothesis-selection lever (orthogonal to width, sampling,
timestamps, prompt slot, and no_repeat_ngram) — the relevant axis for
substitution, which is decided by *which* completed hypothesis wins, not by
how much audio is consumed (length_ratio already healthy at 0.96).
hypothesis:
On the parent (family_003, beam=5, no_speech ablated), raising patience to
2.0 lets the beam search evaluate roughly twice as many completed candidates
before committing, surfacing a higher-scoring transcription on noisy
phone-band Korean audio and lowering the dominant substitution error without
affecting coverage or the sampling-fallback path.
